abaTherapy.title: How ABA Works
abaTherapy.intro: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is an evidence-based approach to understanding and supporting behavior. Here's how the process works at MO Behavior Therapy, from first contact through ongoing care.

sections.title: Initial ABA Assessment
sections.body: A BCBA evaluates your child's needs, behavioral patterns, strengths and your family's priorities to identify potential treatment goals.

sections.title: Functional Behavior Assessment
sections.body: When appropriate, we assess the purpose behind specific behaviors so support strategies address the underlying function, not just the behavior itself.

sections.title: Individualized ABA Therapy
sections.body: Treatment is built from the assessment, with measurable, individualized goals — not a standardized program applied to every child.

sections.title: Treatment Plan Development
sections.body: Goals, strategies and the plan for measuring progress are documented and reviewed with your family.

sections.title: Behavior Intervention Plans
sections.body: When indicated, a plan outlines positive, evidence-based strategies for behaviors that interfere with learning, independence or safety.

sections.title: Data Collection & Progress Monitoring
sections.body: Treatment is continuously reviewed and modified based on data and documented progress — never left on autopilot.

services.title: ABA Services
services.intro: Every family's plan looks different. Not every child receives every service below — your BCBA will recommend what's appropriate based on assessment.

behaviorReduction.title: Behavior Reduction / Behavior Support
behaviorReduction.body: We use positive, evidence-based strategies to address behaviors that interfere with learning, independence or safety — always with respectful, non-stigmatizing language.

parentTraining.title: Parent & Caregiver Training
parentTraining.body: One of the most important parts of treatment. BCBAs collaborate with caregivers so strategies generalize outside therapy sessions.

parentTraining.title: Parent & Caregiver Training
parentTraining.intro: Parent and caregiver involvement is one of the most important parts of ABA treatment. Our BCBAs work directly with families so strategies carry over into daily life — not just therapy sessions.
parentTraining.body: Training is individualized to your family's routines and goals, and may cover communication strategies, positive reinforcement, routines and transitions, and how to respond consistently to challenging moments.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains, in general terms, how MO Behavior Therapy LLC collects, uses and protects information submitted through this website. It is provided for general informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice.

sections.title: Information We Collect
sections.body: We collect information you voluntarily provide through our contact forms, our virtual assistant, and referral or career applications — such as your name, contact details, general location, and general insurance information.

sections.title: How We Use Information
sections.body: Information is used to respond to inquiries, evaluate potential services, coordinate care, and communicate with you about your request. We do not sell your information.

sections.title: Protected Health Information
sections.body: Where information may constitute protected health information, we apply administrative, technical and physical safeguards appropriate to its sensitivity, and we minimize what is collected through public-facing forms and chat.

sections.title: Consent to Contact
sections.body: By submitting a request, you may be asked to separately authorize MO Behavior Therapy to contact you by phone, text or email. This consent is never a condition of receiving services and can be withdrawn at any time.

sections.title: Third-Party Services
sections.body: We may use third-party vendors for functions like email delivery, hosting and analytics. We do not place protected health information into analytics or advertising platforms.

sections.title: Contact Us
sections.body: Questions about this policy can be directed to mobehavior@mobehaviortherapy.com or (305) 795-0600.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.body: MO Behavior Therapy is committed to ensuring this website is accessible to people of all abilities. We aim to meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA guidelines, including keyboard accessibility, appropriate color contrast, semantic structure, and screen-reader-friendly forms and chat controls. If you encounter an accessibility barrier on this site, please contact us at mobehavior@mobehaviortherapy.com or (305) 795-0600 so we can assist you and address the issue.

terms.title: Terms & Website Disclaimer
terms.body: This website is provided for general informational purposes about MO Behavior Therapy LLC and its services. It does not constitute medical advice, and information on this site should not be used to diagnose or treat any condition. Use of the virtual assistant or contact forms does not create a provider-client relationship. Insurance information is general in nature; actual coverage depends on your specific plan and must be verified. For emergencies, call 911 or seek immediate medical attention.

whatIsAba.question: What is ABA therapy?
whatIsAba.answer: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is an evidence-based approach used to understand behavior and teach meaningful skills like communication, social interaction and daily living, based on an individualized assessment.

howToKnowIfAppropriate.question: How do I know if ABA may be appropriate?
howToKnowIfAppropriate.answer: The best way to know is to talk with our team. A BCBA can review your situation and, after an assessment, help determine whether ABA is appropriate and what goals might be recommended.

diagnosisRequired.question: Do I need an autism diagnosis?
diagnosisRequired.answer: Not necessarily to start a conversation with our team — contact us and we can discuss your specific situation and any documentation that may be helpful.

insuranceCoverage.question: Does insurance cover ABA?
insuranceCoverage.answer: Many plans include behavioral health benefits that can apply to ABA, but coverage and authorization requirements vary by plan. Our team can help verify your benefits.

whichPlans.question: Which insurance plans do you work with?
whichPlans.answer: We currently work with Aetna, Florida Blue, Simply Healthcare, UnitedHealthcare and Cigna. Don't see your plan? Contact us — we can review your specific coverage.

howVerificationWorks.question: How does insurance verification work?
howVerificationWorks.answer: After you contact us, our team reviews your insurance information and checks eligibility and behavioral health benefits before any services begin.

whereProvided.question: Where are services provided?
whereProvided.answer: Depending on clinical need and authorization, services may be provided at home, at school, or in the community.

schoolBased.question: Do you provide ABA at school?
schoolBased.answer: We have experience coordinating ABA in school settings when clinically appropriate and authorized by the school or district.

homeBased.question: Do you provide home-based ABA?
homeBased.answer: Yes — many families are served at home, which can make it easier to practice skills within daily routines.

parentTraining.question: What does parent training involve?
parentTraining.answer: Parent and caregiver training is a core part of treatment. BCBAs work directly with families so strategies carry over into everyday life.

whatHappensAtAssessment.question: What happens during an ABA assessment?
whatHappensAtAssessment.answer: A BCBA evaluates your child's needs, behavioral patterns, strengths and your family's priorities to help identify potential treatment goals.

howQuicklyCanStart.question: How quickly can services start?
howQuicklyCanStart.answer: Timing depends on insurance authorization, assessment scheduling and staffing availability — our team can give you a clearer picture once we review your information.

documentsNeeded.question: What documents may be needed?
documentsNeeded.answer: This can vary, but may include a referral, a diagnostic evaluation, or an IEP/504 plan. None of these are required to start a conversation with us.

pediatricianReferral.question: Can my pediatrician send a referral?
pediatricianReferral.answer: Yes — physicians, psychologists and other professionals can refer a client directly to our team through our referral form.

areasServed.question: What areas do you serve?
areasServed.answer: We serve families throughout St. Lucie, Martin, Indian River, Palm Beach, Hendry, Glades, Highlands and Okeechobee counties, with availability varying by location and staffing.

spanishServices.question: Do you provide services in Spanish?
spanishServices.answer: Yes — our team and virtual assistant support Spanish, along with English, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, French and German.

howToRequestServices.question: How can I request services?
howToRequestServices.answer: You can fill out our contact form, chat with our virtual assistant, or call us directly at (305) 795-0600.
